entities.summary:
Aleksander Michał Paweł Sapieha (1734–1793), a scion of the powerful Sapieha family of the Lis coat of arms, stood as a prominent magnate and statesman within the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth during its tumultuous final decades. Serving as Grand Chancellor of Lithuania from 1775 and Grand Hetman of Lithuania from 1792, Sapieha wielded immense political and military influence, becoming a central, albeit often controversial, figure in the struggle between internal reform efforts and the encroaching foreign domination that ultimately led to the Commonwealth's demise.

Sapieha's career was marked by shifting allegiances and a commitment to preserving the traditional liberties of the Polish nobility, often at the expense of necessary state reforms. He began his public service as a voivode of Połock in 1754 and was elected to numerous Sejms, where he frequently opposed measures aimed at strengthening the central government. His elevation to Grand Chancellor in 1775 placed him at the heart of the Commonwealth's legal and administrative apparatus, yet he remained a staunch defender of the magnate oligarchy. During the critical Four-Year Sejm (1788–1792), Sapieha initially supported some reforms but ultimately aligned himself with the conservative opposition, becoming a leading signatory of the Targowica Confederation in 1792, which invited Russian intervention against the Constitution of 3 May.

entities.summary:
Aleksander Michał Paweł Sapieha (1730–1793) emerged as a preeminent magnate within the turbulent political landscape of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth during its final decades, a period marked by profound internal instability and escalating foreign intervention from Russia, Prussia, and Austria. Born into the immensely wealthy and influential Sapieha family of the Lis coat of arms, one of the most powerful princely houses in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, his career unfolded against the backdrop of the First and Second Partitions of Poland. His actions as Grand Chancellor of Lithuania and Grand Hetman of Lithuania were instrumental in shaping the Commonwealth's desperate attempts to preserve its sovereignty, often vacillating between reformist alliances and pro-Russian factions in a bid to secure his family's vast estates and political influence.

Sapieha's political trajectory was characterized by strategic maneuvering within the Sejm and the Senat. Appointed Voivode of Połock in 1754, he ascended to the coveted position of Grand Chancellor of Lithuania in 1775, a role he held until 1792. During the Four-Year Sejm (1788–1792), he initially supported the reformist Constitution of 3 May 1791, which aimed to strengthen the central government and abolish the liberum veto. However, his allegiances shifted dramatically, leading him to join the Targowica Confederation in 1792, a pro-Russian alliance formed to oppose the Constitution and restore the old 'Golden Liberty' of the nobility, effectively inviting Russian military intervention. His final high office was Grand Hetman of Lithuania, a military command he held from 1792 until his death.
